AcceptanceCriterion.description: One acceptance criterion of a session's task.

id.description:
Stable id within the session (`AC1`, or the agent's own), which
walkthroughs and trace scenarios refer to.

text.description: What must hold, one sentence.

updatedAt.description: When it last changed, Unix milliseconds.

path.description: Folder to add. Adding a folder that is already a root is a no-op.

resolve.description: Also resolve the thread (its request is done).

AgentState.description: What an agent session is doing.

oneOf.description: Nothing running; ready for a prompt.
The agent waits for the user's answer to a question.
A permission request waits for the user.
The agent reports it cannot continue without help.
The last turn or the provider failed.

AgentStatus.description:
What the agent says it is doing (`sessions/setStatus`, the `set_status`
MCP tool).

progress.description: Progress, if the work is countable.

state.description: The state the agent claimed with it, if any.

text.description: One short line, at most [`MAX_STATUS_CHARS`] characters.

turn.description: The turn it was set in (`None` between turns).

updatedAt.description: When it was set, Unix milliseconds.

Alert.description: One alert, as it is now.

body.description: More detail (the question, the error), plain text.

createdAt.description: When this occurrence was raised, Unix milliseconds.

dismissed.description: Whether the user dismissed it (hidden from the list).

key.description:
The source's key for it: raising under the same source and key
replaces it. A session's id for the agent sources.

kind.description: How much it wants the user.

read.description: Whether the user has seen it (a resolved alert counts as read).

resolvedAt.description: When the condition cleared, if it has: Unix milliseconds.

session.description: The agent session it is about, if any.

source.description:
The source that raised it: a core source (`agents.permission`,
`agents.question`, `agents.blocked`, `agents.error`, `agents.done`)
or a mod's alert source id.

title.description: One line: "Permission requested: Run cargo test".

updatedAt.description: When it last changed, Unix milliseconds.

workspace.description: The workspace it is about; absent for one about no workspace.

AlertId.description:
Identifies an alert. Assigned by the daemon, never reused; an alert
raised again under its source and key keeps its id.

AlertKind.description: How much an alert wants the user.

oneOf.description:
Something waits for the user: a permission request, a question, a
blocked agent (sand).

alerts.description:
The alerts not dismissed, most recently raised first, at most
[`LIST_LIMIT`].

seq.description:
The `alerts/changes` seq this list reflects; subscribe with
`since: seq` to keep it current.

doNotDisturb.description:
Do not disturb: alerts are still recorded, but nothing pops up
(no toasts, no desktop notifications).

muted.description: Sources that raise nothing, by id.

sources.description: Every source: the core ones, then mods', by id.

AlertSourceInfo.description: A source of alerts, for the per-source settings.

AlertTarget.description: Where opening an alert takes the user, in the alert's workspace.

oneOf.description:
A question an agent asked: its popover in the editor, at
`location` (where the question is pinned, as asked), or the chat.

changed.description: The alerts that changed (each is also an `alerts/changes` event).

AnchorDraft.description:
Lines of a file a step is about, as the file is now (open buffers with
their unsaved edits).

path.description: The file, relative to the root or absolute inside the workspace.

root.description:
Root id from `editor_context`. Default: the scope's root, or the root
an absolute path is in.

AnchorPoint.description:
A spot in a text: 0-based line, byte column within the line and byte
offset from the start (UTF-8, as in `buffer/*`).

offset.description: Byte offset from the start of the text.

buffer.description:
The open buffer `range` is in, if the file is open; else `range` is
in the file on disk.

range.description: Its range in the current text; absent when orphaned.

AnchorSpan.description: A range of a text, `end` exclusive.

AnchorStatus.description: How well an anchor was found in the current text.

oneOf.description: The anchored text, unchanged, in the same place.

The anchored text, unchanged, somewhere else (lines added above, or
the code moved).

Probably the anchored code after an edit; `confidence` in
`0.6..1`.

The code is gone, or no match was good enough. Show the anchor's
own `text`.

AnchorSymbol.description: The innermost symbol an anchor was in (tree-sitter, `coqo-syntax`).

lineOffset.description: How many lines below the symbol's first line the anchor started.

path.description:
Its containers and name, outermost first: `["shapes", "Circle",
"area"]`.

option.description:
The chosen option's id. Required for a confirmation and info; a
decision takes an option, `text`, or both.

text.description: A free-text reply (markdown). Required for a clarification.

anchors.description:
The code it is about: 1 to [`MAX_ANCHORS`] locations, as for
[`Create`].

session.description: The agent session to ask; it must not be running a turn.

AuthKind.description: Where the agent's usage is billed (from ACP `auth/status`).

oneOf.description: A claude.ai (or other) plan login, held by the agent's own CLI.
An API key (Console billing or plan API credits).

AuthStatus.description:
The billing source, for the usage indicator. Carries no identity: Coqo
drops account emails and organizations.

kind.description: What kind of credential is in use.

plan.description: Plan name, if a plan login.

oneOf.description: A GitHub user (the GitHub backend, M8).

AvailableCommand.description: A slash command or skill the agent offers (ACP `available_commands`).

inputHint.description: Placeholder for its argument, if it takes one.

Backend.description: Where a thread lives besides Coqo.

oneOf.description: Only in Coqo: a review of an agent's change, sent to the agent.
A pull request review thread on GitHub (the PR inbox, M8).

BlameHunk.description: Consecutive lines last changed by one commit.

origPath.description: The file's path in that commit, if it was renamed since.

origStart.description: 1-based first line in the file as that commit left it.

path.description: The file, repository-relative.

rev.description:
The revision to blame (default `HEAD`). Uncommitted changes are not
blamed.

commits.description: The commits the hunks name, by id.

hunks.description: Hunks in line order, covering every line.

lineCount.description: Lines in the file at that commit.

name.description: Short name: `main`, or `origin/main` for a remote branch.

time.description: The commit's time, in Unix seconds.

branches.description: Local branches, then remote ones, each by name.

BufferChange.description:
One event of the [`Changes`] topic: a committed change. The event's
subscription `seq` equals `rev`.

clientSeq.description: The replica's `client_seq` for client changes, else 0.

conflict.description:
A disk or agent change that overlapped unsaved edits; both were kept,
and the user should look at the result.

dirty.description: Whether the text differs from the file on disk after this change.

edits.description: The edits, sorted and non-overlapping, against the text at `rev - 1`.

rev.description: The revision this change produced (the previous one plus 1).

BufferId.description:
Identifies an open buffer in the running daemon. Not stable across
daemon restarts or after a buffer is unloaded: reopen by path then.

ByteRange.description: A byte range of the buffer text.

CallResult.description: Result of [`Call`]: what the agent gets back.

isError.description:
Whether the tool failed (invalid arguments, or the mod's error). The
model sees `text` and can correct itself.

structured.description: The result as JSON, if it has one.

text.description: Text for the model: the result, or what went wrong.

path.description: Repository-relative.

workspace.description: The workspace to watch. It must be open.
The workspace to watch. It must be open.

CodeAnchor.description:
Code a question is pinned to, as it was when the agent asked: where,
and a fingerprint to find it again (ADR 0013).

path.description: `/`-separated path relative to the root.

prefix.description: The start of the first line, up to the range.

rev.description:
The buffer revision `range` was taken at; absent for a file read
from disk.

suffix.description: The rest of the last line after the range.

symbol.description: The enclosing symbol, if the file's language is known.

text.description: The anchored text as it was: what to show when it is orphaned.

Color.description: A cell colour. Indexed colours are resolved by the client's theme.

oneOf.description: The 256-colour palette: 0–15 are the ANSI colours.

pending.description: Part of the user's pending review: not sent yet.

CommentId.description:
Identifies a comment, across threads. Assigned by the daemon, never
reused.

comment.description: The comment: one of the user's.

time.description: The author time, in Unix seconds.

message.description: The message. May be empty only when amending (keeps the old one).

group.description:
The name of the group it is listed under, if the agent groups its
entries. Entries of one group are adjacent.

anyOf.description: For a select: one of its entries' `value`.

ConfigValue.description:
A value for `sessions/setConfigOption`: a select entry's `value`, or a
boolean for a toggle.

text.description: The text.

uri.description: Where it came from, if anywhere.

oneOf.description:
A link to a resource the agent can read itself (an `@`-mentioned
file, say).
A resource with its contents embedded (a selection, say).

text.description: Its text.

path.description:
`/`-separated path of the new entry, relative to the root. Missing
folders on the way are created.

root.description: The root the path is relative to.

anchors.description:
The code it is about: 1 to [`MAX_ANCHORS`] locations, the files
as they are now (open buffers with their unsaved edits).

body.description: The question or note, in markdown.

kind.description: What kind of answer it wants; `annotation` for a note.

options.description:
A decision's options (at least 2). Confirmation and info get theirs
from the daemon; the other kinds take none.

walkthrough.description:
The [`WalkthroughDraft`], as the agent wrote it. Checked by the
daemon, which reports every problem at once, so it is any JSON here.

diff.description: The diff source's identity, so the thread can be listed by diff.

lines.description:
The lines (1-based, at most [`MAX_THREAD_LINES`]); omit to comment
on the whole file.

path.description: `/`-separated path of the file, relative to the root.

pending.description:
Add it to the pending review (what the review UI does) rather than
as a comment already made.

side.description: The diff side the user commented on.

version.description:
The version of the file that side shows (see
[`ThreadAnchor::version`]).

cwd.description: The agent's working directory (absolute; the workspace root).

mode.description: Initial mode id, if the provider has modes.

oneOf.description: The session's agent (a session token: the MCP tool).
The user (the daemon token: the UI or the CLI).

CriterionDraft.description: An acceptance criterion a walkthrough addresses.

id.description: Its id: one of the session's (`AC1`) or a new one.

text.description:
What must hold. Default: the session criterion's text; required for
a criterion that is not the session's.

CriterionEvidence.description: Why a criterion has its status: a test, a command, a place in the code.

path.description:
A file that shows it: absolute (a relative path is taken from the
session's `cwd`).

text.description: What shows it, in a few words ("test `volume_discount_caps` passes").

CriterionInput.description:
One entry of `sessions/setCriteria`: a new criterion, or a change to
the one with `id`.

id.description: The criterion to change; a new one gets this id (or `AC<n>`).

status.description: Its status; a new criterion is `pending`.

text.description: Its text; required for a new criterion.

oneOf.description: Verified to hold; the evidence says how.
Cannot be checked here (needs the user, an environment, …).

build.description: The daemon's build id (also in the handshake's `Welcome.build`).

busy.description:
What keeps the daemon busy (agent sessions, traces, …). Busy work
keeps the daemon alive with no clients attached.

connections.description: Clients attached right now, including the one asking.

idle.description: The idle policy and where the daemon is in it.

protocol.description: The protocol version the daemon speaks.

startedAtMs.description: When the daemon started, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

uptimeMs.description: How long the daemon has been running, in milliseconds.

thread.description:
The thread without the comment; absent when it was the last one,
and the thread went with it.

path.description:
The entry to delete (a folder with everything in it). A symlink is
deleted itself, not its target.

permanent.description:
Delete it for good instead of moving it to the OS trash. Without it,
an entry that cannot go to the trash is left alone and the call fails
with [`TRASH_FAILED`](super::codes::TRASH_FAILED).

root.description: The root the path is relative to.

deleteFile.description:
Also delete its committed file, if it has one. Default: the file
stays (it may be committed already; git is the user's).

trashed.description: Whether it went to the OS trash (`false`: deleted for good).

files.description:
The files, sorted by path (`git diff --numstat`). Untracked files
are not on the `worktree` side.

newLine.description: 1-based line on the new side (context and added lines).

newline.description:
`false` for a last line without a line break ("\ No newline at end
of file").

oldLine.description: 1-based line on the old side (context and removed lines).

text.description: The text, without its line break.

base.description:
The old side. Unstaged changes: `index` → `worktree`; staged ones:
`{"rev": "HEAD"}` → `index`.

context.description: Lines of context around changes (default 3, at most 10 000).

path.description: The file, repository-relative.

oneOf.description: The index (what the next commit gets): `"index"`.
A revision: `{"rev": "HEAD"}`, a branch, a commit id, `main~2`, …

DirEntry.description: One entry of a directory listing.

kind.description: What it is. For a symlink, the kind of its target.

mtime.description: Last modification, in Unix milliseconds, if known.

size.description: Size in bytes (of the target, for a symlink; 0 for directories).

symlink.description: Whether the entry itself is a symlink.

discarded.description: How many pending comments were deleted.

workspace.description: Only this workspace's; every alert if absent.

EdgeKind.description: How a graph line meets a row.

oneOf.description:
From lane `from` at the row's top to lane `to` at its bottom,
passing the commit by.
From lane `from` at the row's top into the commit (in lane `to`).

From the commit (in lane `from`) to lane `to` at the row's bottom,
towards a parent.

comment.description: The comment: one of the user's.

EditParams.description: Params of the [`Edit`] notification: one change made by a replica.

baseRev.description: The revision the edits were made against.

clientSeq.description:
Per-replica sequence number, strictly increasing from 1. Resending a
change keeps its seq; the daemon ignores seqs it has committed.

edits.description: The edits, sorted and non-overlapping, against the text at `base_rev`.

replica.description: The replica that made the change.
The replica whose change was rejected.

windows.description:
The windows that show it: the focused one first, then the most
recently updated. Empty when no UI shows the workspace.

EditorTab.description: A file tab open in a window.

active.description:
Whether this is the tab the user works in: the active tab of the
focused pane. At most one per window.

path.description: `/`-separated path relative to the root.

root.description: The root the path is relative to.

selections.description:
Its selections and cursors, the primary one first. Empty if the tab
shows no editor (not loaded yet, or a binary file).

visible.description: The lines on screen, if the tab is visible.

Encoding.description:
How a frame's payload is encoded.

JSON is mandatory and is always used for the handshake. MessagePack is
optional and is switched on for the rest of the connection when both
sides list it in the handshake; it is intended for hot paths (buffer ops,
trace streams).

oneOf.description: MessagePack, with structs encoded as maps keyed by field name.

Anything else: sockets, devices, and symlinks that are broken or point
outside the workspace.

EntryResult.description:
Result of [`Create`] and [`Rename`]: the entry's path, normalised
(`./a//b` is `a/b`).

path.description: `/`-separated path relative to the root.

code.description: One of [`codes`] or an application-defined code.

event.description: The event, shaped by the topic.

subscription.description: The subscription this event belongs to.

workspace.description: Only events of this workspace; omit for every workspace.

FileChange.description: How a path changed on one side.

oneOf.description: Contents or the executable bit changed.
It became another kind of entry (a file became a symlink).

binary.description: Either side is binary (then there are no hunks).

hunks.description: The changes; empty when the contents are equal.

new.description: The new side's file; absent for a deleted file.

old.description: The old side's file; absent for an added file.

path.description: The file, repository-relative.

FileLocation.description: A place in a file of the alert's workspace.

line.description: The 0-based line, if a line is meant.

path.description: `/`-separated path relative to the root.

FileSide.description: A file as one diff side has it.

oid.description: The blob id; absent for a work-tree file.

kind.description: What it is. For a symlink, the kind of its target.

mtime.description: Last modification, in Unix milliseconds, if known.

symlink.description: Whether the path itself is a symlink.

oneOf.description: A comment, or a run of line comments.

FoldingRange.description:
Lines that can be folded: `start_line` stays visible, the lines after it
through `end_line` are hidden.

language.description: The language id, or `null` for plain text.

ranges.description: The ranges, sorted by start line, at most one per line.

Frame.description: What changed on screen since the previous frame.

full.description: The screen starts over (after a resize): rows left out are blank.

FsChanges.description:
One event of the [`Changes`] topic: paths under one root that changed
during a debounce window (about 100 ms).

Paths are reported, not operations: the client re-lists or re-stats them
(a path that no longer exists was removed). Changes deep inside ignored
directories (such as `target/` or `node_modules/`) and inside `.git` are
not reported, but an ignored entry appearing or disappearing directly in
a non-ignored directory is.

paths.description: Changed paths, sorted and without duplicates. Empty when `rescan`.

rescan.description:
Too much changed to report individually (or the watcher lost events):
re-list everything under this root that the client shows.

root.description: The root the paths are relative to.

GitChangeKind.description: What may have changed, in a [`GitChanges`] event.

oneOf.description: Files in the work tree: unstaged changes and untracked files.

GitChanges.description: One event of [`Changes`]: a root's repository may have changed.

kinds.description:
What may have changed, sorted. Status depends on `worktree`,
`index` and `head`; branches on `head` and `refs`; the log on
`head` and `refs`; the stash list on `stash`.

GraphEdge.description: A graph line within one row.

GraphRow.description: The graph at one commit's row. Rows are the same whatever the page.

behind.description: Commits on the upstream the branch lacks.

branch.description: The branch's short name; absent when `HEAD` is detached.

oid.description: The commit; absent on a branch with no commits yet.

Hello.description: Params of `coqo/hello`, sent by the client.

build.description: The client's build id (version + commit), shown in errors and logs.

encodings.description:
Encodings the client accepts after the handshake, in preference
order. JSON is always accepted, even if not listed.

token.description:
The session token that authenticates this client (since 0.1). A
server that authenticates (`coqod` does) rejects a missing or wrong
one with [`codes::UNAUTHORIZED`]. Never logged; servers drop it from
the [`Hello`] they hand to request handlers.

Hunk.description: A run of changes with context, as `git diff` groups them.

newStart.description: First new line (the one before, when `new_lines` is 0).

oldStart.description: First old line (the one before, when `old_lines` is 0).

section.description: The heading after `@@` (the enclosing function, roughly).

IdlePhase.description: Where the daemon is in its idle policy.

oneOf.description: A client is attached or work is busy.
Nothing attached and nothing busy; timers are running.

Idle long enough that services released their resources (language
servers stopped). The daemon exits next, unless it is always on.

IdleStatus.description: The idle policy (PLAN §4.3) and the daemon's current idle phase.

exitAfterSecs.description:
Seconds with no clients and nothing busy before the daemon exits.
`null` means never ("always on").

stopServicesAfterSecs.description:
Seconds with no clients and nothing busy before idle services (such
as language servers) stop. `null` means never.

data.description:
Bytes for the PTY, as text: typed characters, escape sequences for
keys, or pasted text (already wrapped for bracketed paste).

LineEnding.description:
The file's line-ending convention, detected from its first line break.

The buffer text keeps line breaks exactly as they are on disk (mixed
files round-trip unchanged); this tells the editor which break to insert.

oneOf.description: `\n` (also the default for files without line breaks).

LineRange.description: Lines shown in a tab's viewport: 0-based, `end` inclusive.

LineSelection.description:
Lines of one file's diff, by their numbers in it. Choosing a whole hunk
is choosing all its removed and added lines.

entries.description: Entries: directories first, then files, each sorted by name.

includeClosed.description: Answered and dismissed ones too (most recent first, up to 200).

path.description:
…and this file (`/`-separated, relative to `root`; in any root if
`root` is omitted).

root.description: Only questions with an anchor in this root…

diff.description: Only threads started in this diff.

path.description:
…and this file (`/`-separated, relative to `root`; in any root if
`root` is omitted).

ListResult.description: Result of [`List`]: a snapshot of every known workspace.

seq.description:
The event-log `seq` this snapshot reflects. Subscribe to [`Events`]
with `since` set to it to get every later change.

workspaces.description: Every known workspace, most recently opened first.

refs.description: Branches and tags at it (short names), and `HEAD`.

time.description: The author time, in Unix seconds.

revs.description: Start from these revisions (`git log a b`); empty for `HEAD`.

commits.description: Newest first (by committer time, as `git log`).

more.description: More commits follow: ask again with `skip` past these.

session.description:
And every unread alert of this agent session (its chat is on
screen).

Modes.description: Terminal modes that change how a client encodes input.

altScreen.description:
The alternate screen is active (full-screen programs such as `top`);
it has no scrollback, so a client turns wheel scrolling into arrow keys.

appCursor.description: DECCKM: arrow keys send `ESC O A` instead of `ESC [ A`.

mouse.description: The program asked for mouse reports.

NewAnchor.description: A code location to pin a question to: whole lines of a file.

path.description: `/`-separated path of a file relative to the root.

NewOption.description: An option as the agent offers it; the daemon numbers them.

OpenParams.description: Params of [`Open`]. Give exactly one of `path` and `id`.

name.description: Name for a newly created workspace (default: the folder name).

path.description:
Open the workspace for this folder, creating it if needed. A
workspace whose first root is this folder (after canonicalising
the path) is reused, so opening the same folder twice is idempotent.
`/`-separated path of a file relative to the root.

replica.description:
Reuse this replica id (when reopening after a reconnect or a resume
gap), so the daemon reports which of its changes it already has.

root.description: The root the path is relative to.

OpenResult.description: Result of [`Open`]: a snapshot of the buffer.

buffer.description:
The buffer. The same file opened twice (from two windows, or through
a symlink) is the same buffer.

dirty.description: Whether the text differs from the file on disk.

lastSeq.description:
The highest `client_seq` of `replica` the daemon has committed (0 if
none): a pending change with a seq at or below it is already in
`text`.

replica.description: This replica's id: the one asked for, or a new one.

rev.description:
The revision `text` reflects. Subscribe to [`Changes`] with `since`
set to it.

savedRev.description: Revision of the last save or reload from disk.

text.description: The buffer text, including unsaved edits.

Origin.description: Who made a change, with an id whose meaning depends on the kind.

id.description: The source's id, if it has one.

oneOf.description:
An agent; `id` is its session id. Agents' disk writes are attributed
when they match a tool call the daemon was told about.
The file changed on disk (another program, or an unattributed agent).
A formatter run by the daemon.
The buffer was saved: no edits, `dirty` becomes false.

OutlineItem.description: A symbol and the symbols inside it.

children.description: The symbols directly inside it, in document order.

language.description: The language id, or `null` for plain text.

PathParams.description: Params naming a path in a workspace.

path.description: `/`-separated path relative to the root; `""` for the root itself.

root.description: The root the path is relative to.

PendingComment.description: A comment of the pending review, with what it is about.

anchor.description: The code the thread is about, resolved now.

diff.description: The diff the thread was started in.

comments.description: They, by thread (oldest first), then oldest first.

PermissionOption.description: One answer to a permission request.

id.description: Option id, passed back in the outcome.

PermissionOptionKind.description:
What choosing a permission option means (ACP `PermissionOptionKind`).
Auto-approve rules select options by kind, never by label.

PermissionOutcome.description: The answer to a permission request.

oneOf.description: The turn was cancelled (or the session closed) before an answer.

PermissionRequest.description: The agent asks the user to allow something, usually a tool call.

suggestedRule.description:
The workspace rule that answering with `remember: true` creates.
Only offered for requests a rule may answer (a simple command, or
files inside the workspace's roots), and only in a workspace.

title.description: What is asked, such as `Write pong.txt`.

toolCall.description: The tool call it is about, with its diff if it edits a file.

PermissionRequestId.description: Identifies a permission request within a session.

PermissionRule.description:
A per-workspace auto-approve (or auto-reject) rule. Rules answer a
permission request before it reaches the UI; a request no rule matches
is asked. A reject rule wins over an allow rule.

pattern.description: The command prefix or path glob.

PermissionRuleId.description: Identifies a workspace permission rule. Generated by the daemon.

PermissionRuleSpec.description:
What a permission rule matches.

- `execute`: `pattern` is a command prefix, word by word (`cargo test`
  matches `cargo test -p shop` but not `cargo testing`). Only simple
  commands match: no shell operators, redirections, substitutions,
  globs or `~`, no `..`, every absolute path inside the workspace, and
  never programs such as `rm`, `sudo`, `curl` or a shell.
- `edit` and `read`: `pattern` is a glob over paths relative to a
  workspace root (`src/**`, `docs/*.md`); every file the request touches
  must be inside the workspace's roots and match.

pattern.description: The command prefix or path glob.

PlanEntry.description: One entry of the agent's plan (todo list).

Position.description: A place in a text: 0-based line and character (Unicode scalar values).

content.description: The prompt: text, `@`-mentions as resource links, embedded selections.

ProviderAction.description: A button for a provider's setup.

label.description: Button label, such as `Install Claude ACP adapter (npm)`.

oneOf.description:
Open a terminal tab running `program` with `args` in the workspace
(`terminal/spawn`), such as `claude` for the user to `/login`.

embeddedContext.description: Prompts may contain embedded resources (file contents).

resume.description:
Sessions can be reattached after the daemon restarts (ACP
`session/resume` or `session/load`).

ProviderInfo.description: An agent provider, for the chat's provider picker.

available.description:
Whether sessions can be created now: the providing mod is active and
the provider is set up (`status.ready`, when it reports a status).

capabilities.description: What it supports; `null` when not available.

status.description:
Whether it is set up, and what the user can do about it; `null` when
the provider has nothing to report (always ready).

ProviderKind.description: How an agent provider runs (mirrors the mod API's `AgentProviderKind`).

oneOf.description: An ACP agent the daemon runs as a child process.
An unmodified CLI agent in a daemon-owned terminal.
Coqo's own agent loop over a provider's HTTP API.

ProviderStatus.description:
Whether a provider can start sessions on this machine, such as Claude
Code being installed and the ACP adapter set up.

actions.description:
Setup steps the user can take now, such as installing the agent's
adapter. Shown when not ready. Never run without the user asking.

message.description: What is missing or wrong, for the user; `null` when ready.

signIn.description:
How the user signs in to the agent's own tool, offered when a session
fails with `AUTH_REQUIRED`. Coqo never runs a login itself.

context.description:
Its context; `null` when the window closes or stops showing the
workspace.

window.description: The window, unique within the publishing connection.

Question.description: A question or note, as the daemon keeps it.

anchors.description: The code it is about, at least one.

author.description: Who asked: an agent, or the user ([`Ask`]).

body.description: The question or note, in markdown.

kind.description:
What kind of answer it wants (a thread the user started is a
`clarification`).

options.description:
The answers it offers, in order (empty for a clarification or a
note).

session.description:
The agent session that asked (or, for a thread the user started,
the session asked).

severity.description: How important a note is (annotations only).

thread.description:
A thread the user started: their messages, oldest first, each with
the turn that answers it. Empty for an agent's question.

waiting.description:
Whether the agent is blocked on it right now (a waiting
`ask_question` or `await_answer`).

QuestionAnchor.description: One code location of a question.

anchor.description: The code as it was asked about.

text.description: A free-text reply or comment (markdown).

oneOf.description:
The user asked an agent ([`Ask`]): a thread the agent answers in its
session.

QuestionId.description: Identifies a question or note. Assigned by the daemon, never reused.

QuestionKind.description: What kind of answer a question wants (PLAN §7.5), or a note.

oneOf.description: Pick one of the options (or reply in free text).
Yes or no (options `yes` and `no`), with an optional comment.

Something the agent wants the user to see; acknowledge it (option
`ok`).

A non-blocking note pinned to code (`annotate`). Nobody waits for
it; dismiss it when done.

questions.description:
Open questions oldest first, then (with `includeClosed`) closed
ones, most recently closed first.

seq.description:
The `questions/changes` seq this list reflects; subscribe with
`since: seq` to keep it current.

id.description:
What [`AnswerParams::option`] names: `1`, `2`, … for a decision,
`yes` / `no` for a confirmation, `ok` for info.

QuestionStatus.description: Where a question is in its life.

oneOf.description: Waiting for the user (a note: shown until dismissed).
The user dismissed it without an answer.

Range.description: A range of a text. `start` is not after `end`; equal is an empty range.

maxBytes.description:
Fail with [`FILE_TOO_LARGE`](super::codes::FILE_TOO_LARGE) if the
file is larger. Default [`DEFAULT_READ_LIMIT`], at most
[`MAX_READ_LIMIT`].

path.description: `/`-separated path relative to the root.

root.description: The root the path is relative to.

binary.description: Whether the file is not valid UTF-8 (then `text` is absent).

mtime.description: Last modification, in Unix milliseconds, if known.

text.description: The contents, if they are valid UTF-8.

root.description: The root to remove. The last root cannot be removed.

from.description:
The entry to rename or move. A symlink is moved itself, not its
target.

root.description: The root both paths are relative to.

to.description:
Its new path. The folder it goes in must exist, and nothing may be
there yet ([`ALREADY_EXISTS`](super::codes::ALREADY_EXISTS)).

ReplicaId.description:
Identifies one replica of a buffer (one editor in one window), e.g.
`r-3f2a9c1d0b7e4a65`. Assigned by [`Open`]; a replica keeps it across
reconnects and reopens so the daemon can recognise its changes.

pending.description: Add it to the pending review.

prefix.description:
The root's path within the work tree (`""` when the root is the
top). A git path `p` is the root-relative path `p` minus
`prefix + "/"`.

workdir.description: The work tree's top folder, absolute.

RepoParams.description: Params naming a workspace root, whose repository the method acts on.

root.description: The root; its repository is the one whose work tree contains it.

remember.description:
Also create the request's `suggestedRule` in the session's
workspace, allowing or rejecting as the chosen option does. The
chosen option still goes to the agent unchanged.

needed.description: The first sequence number the subscriber needed.

oldest.description: The oldest sequence number still available (`head + 1` if none).

RevealEvent.description: One event of the [`Reveals`] topic: open `path` and select `range`.

path.description: `/`-separated path relative to the root.

range.description: What to show and select; the top of the file if omitted.

root.description: The root the path is relative to.

session.description: The agent session that asked, if an agent did.

path.description: `/`-separated path of a file relative to the root.

range.description: What to show and select; the top of the file if omitted.

root.description: The root the path is relative to.

delivered.description: Whether a UI window shows the workspace, so someone will see it.

workspace.description: Only reveals in this workspace; omit for every workspace.

rev.description: The revision whose change to undo.
The revision of the reverting change.

diff.description: Only comments on threads started in this diff.

Risk.description: Something that could go wrong with a step's code.

text.description: What could go wrong, and what would show it.

RiskSeverity.description: How bad it would be if a risk came true.

oneOf.description: Could break users or data; review closely.

RootId.description:
Identifies a root within its workspace. Stable for the root's lifetime and
never reused within the workspace.

Row.description: One row of the screen, as sparse spans in column order.

row.description: Row index, 0 at the top of the viewport.

RuleDecision.description: Whether a permission rule allows or rejects what it matches.

oneOf.description: Answer with an allow option (`allow_once`, else `allow_always`).
Answer with a reject option (`reject_once`, else `reject_always`).

action.description: A daemon action's id, from the provider's status.

force.description: Overwrite the file even if it changed on disk since it was last read.

savedRev.description: The revision of the save event; the file holds the text as of it.

base.description:
The git revision the change is against (a commit, branch or tag).
Default for `worktree`: `HEAD`. Required for `commits` and `pr`.

head.description:
The last revision of the change. Required for `commits` and `pr`;
not allowed for `worktree`.

kind.description:
`worktree` (uncommitted changes; the usual case right after a
change), `commits` or `pr`.

root.description:
The workspace root (repository) of the change, from
`editor_context`. Default: the first root.

oneOf.description:
The uncommitted changes in the working tree, against `base` (default
`HEAD`). No `head`: the working tree is the head.
A pull request: its base branch `base` and head branch `head`.

Screen.description: The rows in view, the cursor and the modes: what a client draws.

cursor.description: `None` when hidden or scrolled out of view.

display_offset.description: How many lines the viewport is scrolled up into the scrollback.

history_size.description: Lines of scrollback above the screen.

ScrollTo.description: How to move a terminal's viewport through its scrollback.

oneOf.description: Up into the scrollback by this many lines (negative: down).

Selection.description: A selection or cursor in a tab.

range.description: The selected range; empty for a cursor.

text.description:
The selected text, for a non-empty selection, at most
[`MAX_SELECTION_TEXT`] bytes.

diff.description: Only comments on threads started in this diff.

session.description:
The agent session to send them to: one of the workspace's, not in a
turn.

count.description: How many comments were sent (no longer pending).

SessionConfigOption.description:
A setting the agent offers for the session (ACP session config
options): the model, the reasoning effort, a fast-mode toggle, the mode,
an agent persona, …. The agent decides which there are and their order;
they can change at any time (a new model may offer other efforts), and
every [`SessionUpdate::ConfigOptions`] replaces the whole list.

oneOf.description: One value of a list (a dropdown).

options.description: The entries, in the agent's order.

category.description:
What the option is about, for placement and icons only: ACP's
[`config_category`] names (`mode`, `model`, `model_config`,
`thought_level`, `speed`) or any other string. Never needed to use
the option.

SessionId.description: Identifies an agent session. Generated by the daemon; stable forever.

criteria.description: The task's acceptance criteria, in order (`sessions/setCriteria`).

cwd.description: The agent's working directory (the workspace root).

mode.description: Current mode id, if the provider has modes.

stateSince.description:
When `state` last changed, Unix milliseconds (how long it has
waited, for alerts and the agents overview).

status.description:
What the agent says it is doing, if it said so this turn (or its
`blocked` or `done` outcome).

title.description: Title for tabs and the sidebar.

toolUse.description:
The tools the agent called this session and how often, in order of
first use, counted from its tool calls (live ones, not replays).

updatedAt.description: Last change to this info, Unix milliseconds.

workspace.description: The workspace it belongs to, if any.

seq.description:
The `sessions/changes` seq this list reflects; subscribe with
`since: seq` to keep it current.

SessionMode.description:
A session mode, such as Claude Code's `default` ("Manual"),
`acceptEdits` or `plan`.

SessionModes.description:
The session's modes. Whether a permission prompt appears depends on the
mode, so the UI always shows it.

SessionSnapshot.description:
One session's folded state: what a chat tab shows before replaying the
transcript.

configOptions.description:
The session's config options (model, effort, …), in the agent's
order. Empty if the provider has none.

head.description:
Seq of its last update (0 if none). Subscribe to `sessions/updates`
with `since: head` to continue from here.

pendingPermissions.description: Permission requests waiting for an answer.

SessionToken.description:
A secret that authenticates a connection: the daemon's per-boot token,
or a token scoped to one workspace and agent session.

It is a string on the wire. `Debug` prints `SessionToken(<redacted>)`
and equality is constant-time, so the token neither leaks into logs nor
through comparison timing. Use [`SessionToken::expose`] only to send or
store it.

SessionUpdate.description:
One entry of a session's transcript: an event of `sessions/updates`.

Updates from the agent mirror ACP `session/update`; the rest are written
by the daemon (prompts, turns, permissions, state).

oneOf.description:
Part of a user message replayed by the agent (when Coqo rebuilds a
transcript it lost from the agent's own history).
Streaming agent output; consecutive chunks form one message.
A change to a tool call.
The agent's plan; replaces the earlier plan.
The agent's slash commands and skills; replaces the earlier list.

The session's config options, with their current values; replaces
the earlier list (an empty list: none).

configOptions.description: Every option, in the agent's order.

oneOf.description: The agent asks for permission; answer with `sessions/respondPermission`.
A permission request was answered or cancelled.

byRule.description:
The workspace rule that answered it without asking. It follows
its `permission_requested` at once; the state stays `working`.

remembered.description:
The rule the user's answer created ("remember for this
workspace").

oneOf.description:
A question or note the agent pinned to code (`questions/*`), as
asked, and again when it is answered or dismissed: the chat shows
it with links to its code.

The agent published a code walkthrough (`walkthroughs/*`): the chat
shows a card that opens it where it starts.
The session was closed. Nothing follows.

configId.description: The option's id, from the session's config options.

value.description: The new value: a select entry's `value`, or a boolean for a toggle.

criteria.description: New criteria and changes, in order.

replace.description:
The list becomes exactly `criteria`, in that order: criteria not
named are dropped, named ones keep what their entry does not change.
Otherwise an entry with a known id changes that criterion in place
and the others are added at the end.

modeId.description: The mode id, from the session's modes.

value.description: The new value; `null` removes the entry.

progress.description: Progress (`total` at least 1; `current` is capped at `total`).

state.description:
The state the agent claims: `working` clears an earlier `blocked`,
`blocked` asks for the user (the status says why), `done` marks the
task finished (the session is `done` once the turn ends).

status.description:
One short line (whitespace is collapsed; cut at
[`MAX_STATUS_CHARS`]). Must not be empty.

state.description: Where the reader is with it.

force.description: Stop even if work is busy.

busy.description: When not stopping: the busy work that kept it running.

stopping.description:
Whether the daemon is stopping. It closes every connection and exits
shortly after answering.

Span.description:
A run of cells with one style, starting at column `col`. Each character
of `text` takes one cell, or two in a `wide` span (CJK, emoji). Blank
default-styled cells are left out.

wide.description: Every character is two cells wide.

cwd.description: Working directory. Omit for the user's home directory.

env.description: Extra environment variables, on top of the daemon's environment.

program.description: The program to run. Omit for the user's login shell.

title.description: Tab title until the program sets one. Defaults to the program name.

lines.description:
Only these lines of the file's diff: for [`Stage`] the unstaged
diff (`index` → `worktree`), for [`Unstage`] the staged one
(`HEAD` → `index`), both with 3 lines of context. Lines that are not
in the current diff fail with
[`STALE_SELECTION`](super::codes::STALE_SELECTION).

message.description: As `git stash list` shows it: `On main: message`.

time.description: When it was made, in Unix seconds.

created.description: `false` if there was nothing to stash.

conflict.description: Set for an unmerged path (then `staged` and `unstaged` are absent).

path.description:
Repository-relative. An untracked folder git does not look into (a
nested repository) ends in `/`.

StatusState.description: The state an agent claims with its status (`set_status`).

oneOf.description: Cannot continue without the user; the status says why.
The task is finished; the status is the outcome.

Step.description: One step of a stored walkthrough.

anchors.description: The code, at least one location.

title.description: The step in a few words.

why.description: Why it is done this way (markdown).

StepAnchor.description: One code location of a step.

resolution.description:
Where it is now: set by [`Get`], absent elsewhere (and in committed
files).

StepDraft.description: One step of a walkthrough: code to read, and what, why and the risks.

anchors.description: The code the step is about: 1 to 16 line ranges.

criteria_refs.description: The acceptance criteria (ids) this step helps meet.

depends_on.description: Steps (ids) to read before this one.

id.description:
Unique within the walkthrough (letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`; at
most 32), for `depends_on`: `s1`, `discount-rule`.

title.description: The step in a few words.

why.description:
Why it is done this way: the reasoning, the alternatives turned
down.

StepKind.description: What a step is about, so the reader knows where they are.

oneOf.description: Where the change is entered: a route, a command, a public function.
How control or data moves from there.
Types, schemas, structs the change adds or alters.
The core logic: rules, calculations, decisions.
Limits, errors, empty and concurrent cases.
Tests that show the change works.
Configuration, flags, build or dependency changes.

StepState.description: Where the reader is with one step (the player's progress).

oneOf.description: The reader has a question about it.

StopReason.description: Why a turn ended (ACP `StopReason`, plus Coqo's own).

oneOf.description: The per-turn request limit was reached.
The provider failed; see the turn's `error`.
The daemon stopped during the turn.
In the daemon only, private to the user.

Also written to `.coqo/walkthroughs/<id>.json` in the repository,
for the user to commit.

Style.description: How a run of cells is drawn.

since.description: Resume after this sequence number; omit for live events only.

head.description: The source's latest sequence number when the subscription started.

SubscriptionId.description: Identifies a subscription on one connection.

name.description:
A local branch, or a remote branch's name without the remote (git
then creates a tracking branch).

Symbol.description: A named definition: a function, method, type, module, heading, key, …

container.description:
Names of the symbols that contain this one, outermost first: a method
`area` in `impl Circle` inside `mod shapes` has `["shapes", "Circle"]`.

endLine.description: Last line of the definition (0-based, inclusive).

name.description: The name, with runs of whitespace collapsed to one space.

oneOf.description: A class (also a Kotlin `object` or a Java record).
An interface or a Java annotation type.
An `impl` block; its name is the implementing type.
A function inside a class, struct, trait, interface, impl or object.
A key in a data file (JSON, YAML, TOML).
A CSS rule, at-rule or keyframe.

language.description: The language id (`rust`, `tsx`, …), or `null` for plain text.

symbols.description: Every symbol, in document order (a container before what it holds).

oneOf.description: The program set the title (OSC 0/2), or reset it.
The shell reported a new working directory (OSC 7).
The shell reported a finished command (OSC 133;D).

The process exited. The terminal stays until [`Close`] so its last
output can still be read.

TerminalId.description: Identifies a terminal for the lifetime of the daemon.

TerminalInfo.description: What the daemon knows about a terminal.

cwd.description:
The working directory: as reported by the shell (OSC 7), else the
process's own (where the OS can tell), else the spawn directory.

last_command_exit.description: Exit code of the last shell command, if the shell reports it (OSC 133;D).

pid.description: Process id of the program (also its process group).

title.description: The title: set by the program (OSC 0/2), else the spawn title.

seq.description: The [`Output`] seq this snapshot reflects: subscribe with `since: seq`.

TerminalStatus.description: Whether a terminal's process is still running.

oneOf.description: The process exited. `code` is `None` when a signal ended it.

end.description: One past the last byte replaced; `start` for a pure insert.

start.description: First byte replaced (UTF-8 offset, on a character boundary).

text.description: The replacement.

TextEncoding.description:
The file's text encoding. Only UTF-8 is supported for now; other files
fail to open with [`UNSUPPORTED_ENCODING`](super::codes::UNSUPPORTED_ENCODING).

oneOf.description:
UTF-8 with a byte-order mark. The mark is not part of the buffer text
and is written back on save.

comments.description: The comments, oldest first; at least one.

diff.description:
The diff it was started in (a diff source's identity, such as
`git:0:index..worktree`), if any.

ThreadAnchor.description: The code a thread is about.

code.description:
The lines as they were when the thread was started; absent for a
thread on the whole file.

lines.description:
The lines now, 1-based; as they were when orphaned. Absent for a
thread on the whole file.

path.description: `/`-separated path of the file, relative to the root.

resolution.description:
Where `code` is in `version` now (absent with `code`). Its range
is never in an open buffer: it is in the version as git sees it.

side.description: The diff side it was started on.

version.description:
The version of the file the lines are in: `worktree` for the new
side of unstaged changes, `index` for their old side, `{"rev":
"HEAD"}`, … A diff shows the thread on whichever side shows this
version.

oneOf.description: A thread was created or changed: its state now.
A thread was deleted (its last comment was).

ThreadId.description: Identifies a thread. Assigned by the daemon, never reused.

ThreadLines.description: Lines of a file, 1-based, `end` inclusive (as diffs number them).

seq.description:
The `threads/changes` seq this list reflects; subscribe with
`since: seq` to keep it current.

threads.description: The threads, oldest first, open and resolved.

ThreadMessage.description: One message the user sent in a thread ([`Ask`], [`Reply`]).

text.description: The message, markdown.

turn.description: The session turn it started: the agent's reply is that turn.

ThreadSide.description: The side of a diff a thread was started on.

oneOf.description: The base (removed lines, the old line numbers).
The head (added lines, the new line numbers).

ThreadStatus.description: Whether a thread still needs attention.

ToolCall.description: A tool call, as first reported.

name.description:
The tool's name as the agent calls it, if the agent says (`Read`,
`mcp__coqo-editor__ask_question`). The Claude adapter sends it as
`_meta.claudeCode.toolName`. Tool-use stats count by it.

ToolCallContent.description: What a tool call produced or proposes.

oneOf.description:
A file edit. For ACP agents it arrives *before* the write (and before
the permission request), which is what inline accept/reject uses.

oldText.description: The text before; `null` for a new file.

path.description: Absolute path of the file.

oneOf.description: A daemon terminal the tool runs in.

ToolCallId.description: Identifies a tool call within a session.

ToolCallLocation.description: A file location a tool call touches, for follow-along.

path.description: Absolute path.

ToolCallStatus.description: Where a tool call is in its lifecycle.

oneOf.description: Not started (input still streaming, or waiting for permission).

ToolCallUpdate.description:
A change to a tool call. Fields left out are unchanged; `content` and
`locations` replace the earlier lists when present.

ToolGroup.description: Which kind of tool a call used, for tool-use stats.

oneOf.description:
A core tool of Coqo's `coqo-editor` MCP server (`editor_context`,
`ask_question`, ...; [`super::mcp::CORE_TOOLS`]).
A tool a Coqo mod contributes through `coqo-editor`.
A tool of another MCP server (the user's own).

description.description: What it does, for the agent.

inputSchema.description: JSON Schema of the arguments (an object schema).

name.description: The name agents see: 1 to 64 of `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -`.

ToolKind.description: What kind of tool a call is, for icons and grouping (ACP `ToolKind`).

ToolUse.description: How often a session called one tool.

group.description: Which kind of tool it is.

name.description:
The tool: its own name for `coqo-editor` tools (`ask_question`),
else the name the agent calls it by (`Read`,
`mcp__github__get_issue`). Tool calls whose agent gives no name
count by their kind (`edit`).

ToolsChangedEvent.description: One event of [`ToolsChanged`]: the set of tools changed; list again.

generation.description: How many times the set changed since the daemon started.

workspace.description: The workspace the tools are for.

TrivialHunk.description: A changed hunk the agent marked as needing no explanation.

lines.description:
The hunk's lines in the new file, 0-based, `end` inclusive; absent
for the whole file.

path.description: `/`-separated path relative to the root.

TrivialHunkDraft.description: A changed hunk that needs no explanation.

path.description:
The file, relative to the root or absolute inside the workspace. It
may be deleted.

root.description:
Root id. Default: the scope's root, or the root an absolute path is
in.

start_line.description:
First line of the hunk (1-based, in the new file). Default: the
whole file.

UncoveredHunk.description: A changed hunk no step covers and no trivial hunk lists.

excerpt.description: The first changed lines, `+` added and `-` removed, a few at most.

newRange.description:
Where it is in the new file, 0-based, `end` inclusive: its lines,
or for lines only removed, the line before them (the first line
when they were at the top). This is where to open it; `{0, 0}` for
a deleted file.

oldRange.description:
The removed lines in the old file, 0-based, `end` inclusive; absent
when lines were only added.

path.description: `/`-separated path relative to the root (the new path of a rename).

renamedFrom.description: The old path of a rename.

wholeFile.description: Set when the hunk is a whole file (added, deleted, binary, renamed).

contextSize.description: The model's context size in tokens.

cost.description:
Cost reported by the agent. On a subscription plan this is the SDK's
notional figure, **not** a charge; show it only with
[`AuthStatus::kind`] `api_key` / `external`.

coverage.description:
How much of the scope's diff the steps cover. Computed when
published, and again by `get` for a worktree scope (the work tree
changes); absent from walkthroughs published before it existed.

stepStates.description:
The reader's progress by step id; a step not listed is unread. Never
written to committed files.

summary.description: The change in a few sentences (markdown).

title.description: What changed, in a few words.

agent.description: Its provider (`claude-code`), or `agent` if the session is unknown.

summary.description: It as it is now; absent when deleted.

WalkthroughCoverage.description:
How much of a walkthrough scope's diff its steps cover.

Every changed hunk of the scope (`git diff` without context, so each run
of changed lines is one hunk; untracked files count for a worktree
scope) is **covered** when a step's anchor overlaps its lines in the new
file (lines only removed: an anchor on the line before or after them),
else **trivial** when `trivial_hunks` lists it (by the same overlap, or
the whole file), else **uncovered**.

unavailable.description:
Why the diff could not be computed (not a git repository, git
unavailable, no commits yet); the counts are 0 then.

uncovered.description:
The uncovered hunks (`total - covered - trivial` of them), at most
[`MAX_UNCOVERED`] (a summary: [`SUMMARY_UNCOVERED`]).

WalkthroughCriterion.description:
An acceptance criterion a walkthrough addresses, as it was when it was
published. Steps refer to it by `id`; the session's live criteria (ADR
0017) say whether it holds now.

status.description:
Its status in the session when published; absent for a criterion
only the walkthrough names.

text.description: What must hold.

WalkthroughDraft.description:
A code walkthrough as an agent publishes it with `publish_walkthrough`:
the change in the order a reader should follow it (entry point → flow →
data → logic → edge cases → tests), every step anchored to code. Coqo
fills in the id, the author and the time. Lines are 1-based.

acceptance_criteria.description:
The acceptance criteria the change addresses, by id. Default: every
criterion of this session (`set_acceptance_criteria`). A criterion
that is not the session's needs `text`.

require_coverage.description:
Refuse to publish while a changed hunk of the scope is neither in a
step's anchors nor in `trivial_hunks` (each is listed). Default:
publish, and list the uncovered hunks in the result and to the
reader.

steps.description: The steps, in reading order: 1 to 100.

summary.description:
The change in two to five sentences (markdown): what it does and
why.

title.description: What changed, in a few words ("Volume discount for bulk orders").

trivial_hunks.description:
Changed hunks no step needs to explain (formatting, imports,
renames), so the coverage check does not flag them.

WalkthroughDraft.title: Coqo walkthrough

WalkthroughId.description:
Identifies a walkthrough: a slug of its title and a random suffix, e.g.
`volume-discount-3f2a9c1b`. Assigned by the daemon; also the committed
file's name.

WalkthroughLocation.description: A file location, for opening a walkthrough where it starts.

lines.description: The anchored lines when published, 0-based, `end` inclusive.

path.description: `/`-separated path relative to the root.

WalkthroughProblem.description: One thing wrong with a draft.

message.description: What is wrong and how to fix it.

path.description:
Where, as a JSON path into the draft: `steps[2].anchors[0].end_line`
(empty for the whole draft).

problems.description: Every problem found, in document order.

WalkthroughScope.description: What a stored walkthrough covers, with its revisions resolved.

base.description: The base revision as the agent named it (`HEAD`, `main`).

baseCommit.description: The base commit when published (absent outside a git repository).

head.description: The head revision as named; absent for the working tree.

headCommit.description: The head commit when published; absent for the working tree.

kind.description: Worktree, commits or a pull request.

root.description: The workspace root (repository) of the change.

error.description:
Why the committed file could not be written; the walkthrough is kept
locally anyway.

path.description:
The committed file, relative to the scope's root
(`.coqo/walkthroughs/<id>.json`).

WalkthroughSummary.description: A walkthrough in a list, the transcript and change events.

coverage.description:
How much of the diff the steps cover, with at most
[`SUMMARY_UNCOVERED`] of the uncovered hunks listed.

questions.description: How many are marked with a question.

scope.description: Worktree, commits or a pull request.

start.description: The first step's first anchor, where a reader starts.

session.description: The watching agent session: the one that asked.

Welcome.description: Result of `coqo/hello`, sent by the server.

build.description:
The server's build id. Equal builds are compatible by definition;
different builds are compatible when the protocol versions are.

connection.description: A server-assigned id for this connection, unique per server process.

encoding.description: The encoding both sides use from the next frame on.

negotiated.description: The negotiated version for this connection.

WholeFile.description: A changed file a hunk stands for as a whole.

oneOf.description: The file is new (all its lines are one hunk).
The file is gone: only `trivial_hunks` can cover it.
Either side is binary (no lines): only `trivial_hunks` can cover it.
Moved, contents unchanged; `renamedFrom` has the old path.

WindowContext.description: One window's editor context for the workspace it shows.

focused.description: Whether the window has the keyboard focus.

tabs.description: Its file tabs, in tab order.

WindowState.description: A window's context as the daemon keeps it.

focused.description: Whether the window has the keyboard focus.

tabs.description: Its file tabs, in tab order.

updatedAtMs.description: When it last published, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

window.description: The window, as its UI named it.

oneOf.description: A workspace was opened (or created and opened).
A workspace's name or roots changed.
A workspace was removed (forgotten; its folders are untouched).
A state entry was set or removed.

value.description: The new value; `null` if it was removed.

WorkspaceId.description: Stable identifier of a workspace, e.g. `ws-3f2a9c1d0b7e4a65`.

WorkspaceInfo.description: A workspace as the daemon knows it.

createdAt.description: When the workspace was created, in Unix milliseconds.

lastOpenedAt.description: When the workspace was last opened, in Unix milliseconds.

open.description: Whether the workspace is open (watched, shown in the rail).

roots.description: Folder roots, in display order. Never empty.

WorkspaceRoot.description: One folder root of a workspace.

id.description: The root's id within the workspace.

name.description: Display name (the folder name by default).

path.description: Absolute, canonical path of the folder.

WorkspaceState.description:
A workspace's persisted state document, e.g. `tabs`, `layout`,
`settings`. The keys and values belong to the UI; the daemon only stores
them.

title: Coqo Protocol
x-framing: u32 big-endian payload length, then one JSON-RPC 2.0 message (JSON, or MessagePack if negotiated)

agents/deletePermissionRule.description: Delete a permission rule. Result is true if it existed.

agents/permissionRules.description: A workspace's permission rules (auto-approve and auto-reject), oldest first.

agents/providers.description: Every agent provider, with whether it is available.

agents/runAction.description: Run a provider's setup action (such as installing its adapter) at the user's request.

alerts/changes.description: Alerts whose state changed, as their latest state (resumable).

alerts/dismissAll.description: Hide every alert, or a workspace's.

alerts/list.description: The alerts not dismissed, newest first, with the changes seq.

alerts/markRead.description: Mark alerts (or an agent session's) read.

alerts/settings.description: Do-not-disturb and the alert sources, muted or not.

buffer/changes.description: Every committed change of a buffer; seq is the buffer rev (resumable with since).

buffer/close.description: A replica is done with a buffer; it unloads once unsubscribed.

buffer/edit.description: A replica's change against base_rev; acknowledged by its own buffer/changes event.

buffer/editRejected.description: A buffer/edit the daemon could not apply; reopen the buffer.

buffer/open.description: Open (or join) the buffer of a file: text, rev and a replica id.

buffer/revertChange.description: Undo one change (typically an agent's), transformed past later changes.

buffer/save.description: Write the buffer to its file atomically.

coqo/hello.description: Handshake. Always the first request, always JSON.

coqo/subscribe.description: Start a subscription to a topic.

coqo/subscriptionEnded.description: The server ended a subscription, with an error if abnormal.

coqo/unsubscribe.description: Stop a subscription. Result is true if it existed.

daemon/shutdown.description: Stop the daemon. Refused while work is busy unless `force` is set.

daemon/status.description: Daemon version, pid, uptime, attached clients, busy work and idle policy.

editor/context.description: A UI window's editor context (tabs, selections, visible lines) for its workspace.

editor/getContext.description: What the windows showing a workspace have open, focused window first.

editor/reveal.description: Ask the UI to open a file and select a range.

editor/reveals.description: Reveal requests for UIs to act on (live only).

fs/changes.description: Debounced file-system changes in an open workspace (live only).

fs/create.description: Create an empty file or a folder in a workspace root (daemon token only).

fs/delete.description: Move an entry to the OS trash, or delete it for good with permanent (daemon token only).

fs/list.description: List a directory in a workspace root.

fs/read.description: Read a file in a workspace root, up to a size limit.

fs/rename.description: Rename or move an entry within a workspace root; open buffers follow it (daemon token only).

fs/stat.description: Metadata of one path in a workspace root.

git/blame.description: Which commit last changed each line of a file.

git/changes.description: A root's repository may have changed: work tree, index, HEAD, refs or stash (live only).

git/commit.description: Commit what is staged, or amend.

git/createBranch.description: Create a branch, and optionally switch to it.

git/diff.description: One file's hunks between two sides (work tree, index, a revision).

git/diffFiles.description: The files that differ between two sides, with line counts.

git/log.description: Commits newest first, a page at a time, with graph lanes.

git/stage.description: Stage whole files, or chosen lines of one file.

git/stashApply.description: Apply a stash and keep it.

git/stashPop.description: Apply a stash and drop it.

git/status.description: A root's repository: branch and changed paths.

git/unstage.description: Unstage whole files, or chosen lines of one file.

mcp/call.description: Call a mod-contributed MCP tool for an agent session.

mcp/tools.description: The MCP tools mods contribute, as the coqo-editor bridge offers them.

mcp/toolsChanged.description: The mod-contributed MCP tools changed; list them again (live only).

questions/ask.description: The user asks an agent session about code: a thread pinned to it.

questions/changes.description: Questions whose state changed, as their latest state (resumable).

questions/create.description: An agent asks a question or adds a note pinned to code.

questions/dismiss.description: Close a question without an answer, or a note.

questions/list.description: A workspace's questions and notes, anchors resolved now, with the changes seq.

questions/reply.description: A follow-up in a thread the user started.

questions/watch.description: One question for the agent that asked: its state now, then every change.

review/pending.description: The user's pending review: the comments not sent yet.

review/reply.description: An agent session replies in a review thread of its workspace, optionally resolving it.

review/send.description: Send the pending review to an agent session in one prompt, then clear pending.

sessions/cancel.description: Cancel the running turn. Result is true if one was running.

sessions/changes.description: The latest info of each session whose state, title or mode changed (resumable).

sessions/close.description: End a session; its transcript stays readable. Result is true if it was open.

sessions/create.description: Start an agent session with a provider.

sessions/get.description: One session's folded state and the seq of its last update.

sessions/list.description: Agent sessions, with the sessions/changes seq the list reflects.

sessions/prompt.description: Start a turn; it runs in the daemon and streams on sessions/updates.

sessions/setConfigOption.description: Change one of a session's config options (model, effort, a toggle, …).

sessions/setCriteria.description: Set or update the session's acceptance criteria (session tokens: own session).

sessions/setStatus.description: The agent's status line, progress and claimed state (session tokens: own session).

sessions/updates.description: One session's persisted transcript (resumable with since; seqs per session).

syntax/folding.description: The foldable line ranges of an open buffer.

syntax/outline.description: The symbols of an open buffer as a tree.

syntax/symbols.description: Every symbol of an open buffer (tree-sitter tags), flat, with container paths.

terminal/close.description: Kill a terminal's process group and forget it. True if it existed.

terminal/input.description: Write to a terminal's PTY. Send the next one after this one's response.

terminal/output.description: A terminal's changed rows (batched at ~60 Hz), title, cwd and exit.

terminal/scroll.description: Move a terminal's viewport through its scrollback.

terminal/snapshot.description: A terminal's screen and the terminal/output seq it reflects.

terminal/spawn.description: Start a program (or the login shell) in a new daemon-owned PTY.

threads/changes.description: Threads whose state changed, as their latest state, and deleted ones (resumable).

threads/create.description: Start a thread on lines of a file version (or the whole file).

threads/deleteComment.description: Delete one of the user's comments; an empty thread goes with it.

threads/editComment.description: Change one of the user's comments.

threads/list.description: A workspace's comment threads, anchors resolved now, with the changes seq.

threads/reply.description: Add the user's comment to a thread.

walkthroughs/changes.description: Walkthroughs published, updated or deleted (live only).

walkthroughs/create.description: An agent publishes a walkthrough; every problem of a bad draft is reported at once.

walkthroughs/delete.description: Forget a walkthrough (and optionally its committed file).

walkthroughs/get.description: One walkthrough, anchors resolved against the files as they are now.

walkthroughs/setStepState.description: Mark a step unread, understood or with a question.

workspace/addRoot.description: Add a folder root to a workspace.

workspace/events.description: Workspace changes, from the persistent event log (resumable with since).

workspace/getState.description: A workspace's persisted state document (tabs, layout, settings overrides).

workspace/list.description: Every known workspace, with the event-log seq the snapshot reflects.

workspace/open.description: Open (creating if needed) the workspace for a folder, or reopen one by id.

workspace/remove.description: Forget a workspace and its daemon-side data. Result is true if it existed.

workspace/removeRoot.description: Remove a folder root from a workspace.

workspace/setState.description: Set (or, with null, remove) one workspace state entry.
